status_summary: Bills to repeal the charter were introduced on 2025-07-16: H.R. 4450 (Rep. Mark Harris, 14 original cosponsors, referred to the House Judiciary Committee) and S. 2310 (Sen. Marsha Blackburn with Sen. Cynthia Lummis, referred to the Senate Judiciary Committee), each titled the National Education Association Charter Repeal Act and each repealing chapter 1511 of title 36, U.S. Code. A bill tracker lists 18 cosponsors on the House bill and shows no committee action or vote on either bill. The House Education and Workforce Committee wrote to the NEA on 2025-09-29 opening an inquiry into its retirement program, with documents due 2025-10-13; that letter concerns member retirement products and not federal funds, and no hearing on NEA use of federal money was found.

timeline.event: H.R. 4450, the National Education Association Charter Repeal Act, was introduced by Rep. Mark Harris with 14 cosponsors and referred to the House Judiciary Committee; it would repeal chapter 1511 of title 36, U.S. Code.
S. 2310, the Senate companion, was introduced by Sen. Marsha Blackburn for herself and Sen. Cynthia Lummis and referred to the Senate Judiciary Committee.
The House Education and Workforce Committee majority wrote to the NEA president opening an investigation of the NEA's retirement program and requested documents by 2025-10-13.
timeline.source: House Committee on Education and Workforce

title: Repeal the National Education Association's federal charter and hold hearings on its funds
uncertainties: Cosponsor count after introduction (18) and committee status come from a bill tracker (policysoup.com); congress.gov action pages could not be fetched (robots restriction), so later actions are not confirmed from a primary source. The STUDENT Act named in an earlier lead was not found. An earlier version of the repeal bill in the 118th Congress was seen only in a search result list and is not used. The Education and Workforce letter concerns retirement product fees and not federal funds; the Walberg office page dated 2025-10-01 reports the same letter. No hearing specifically on NEA use of federal funds was found.
